## Brand Strategy
- **Brand truths:** Collective power is the central narrative -- "whatever the challenge, our collective strength means we rise to it together."
- **Architecture philosophy:** Single unified logo across all divisions. No sub-brands, no divisional logos. Complexity managed through an "information system" device rather than separate brands.
- **Positioning:** Specialism meets scale. Compelling alternative in a consolidated insurance market.

## Logo
- **Primary mark:** "Howden" wordmark that is simultaneously a symbol -- letterforms come together to create a single, unified mark.
- **Logo expressions:**
  - Solid colour (most common usage)
  - Lens effect: logo sits on photography and shows photography within it
  - Lens on white: photography/gradient inside logo on white background (large scale only)
  - Gradient: logo holds three-color gradients
  - Atmospheric: for mood-setting applications
  - Colour on photography: solid colour logo overlaid on photos
- **Clear space:** 50% of symbol height on all sides.
- **Colour use hierarchy:** Primary = hero pairings (Moss green/Pistachio, Cobalt blue/Teal, Rosewood/Poppy). Secondary = white on dark/photo. Tertiary = Moss green or black on light backgrounds.
- **Core pairings:** Eight documented foreground/background combinations from full palette.
- **Logo crops:** Portions of the logo used as graphic device, with tint and contrast variations.

## Typography
- **Primary typeface:** GT Ultra Median Regular -- contemporary, friendly, characterful serif. Used for headings, titles, information system, and pull quotes.
- **Secondary typeface:** Aktiv Grotesk (Regular, Semi-Bold) -- highly legible sans serif in Latin and nine non-Latin scripts. Used for body copy, functional text, data labels.
- **System fonts:** Georgia Regular (headings), Arial Regular (body) -- for emails, letters, day-to-day where brand fonts unsupported.
- **Hierarchy:** Three levels -- (1) GT Ultra Median headings, (2) GT Ultra Median sub-headings/pull quotes, (3) Aktiv Grotesk body copy.
- **Sizing system:** Multiples of 9pt (108, 81, 63, 45, 27, 18pt headings; 13.5pt and 9pt body). Leading: 120% below 75pt, 110% above 75pt.
- **Tabs expression:** Words repositioned within titles to break up long headings, aligned to grid thirds. Tabbed words may change colour for emphasis.
- **Language support:** GT Ultra Median for Latin; Aktiv Grotesk Medium for non-Latin headings (Arabic, Thai, Hebrew, etc.). CJK requires separate license.
- **Scaling rules:** A4 as reference point; type size rounded to nearest multiple of 9pt when scaling.
- **Body copy:** Recommended 9.5pt/13pt leading. Ideal 35-60 characters per line.

## Color
- **Primary palette (8 colors):**
  - Poppy: #F9423A / PMS Warm Red / RAL 3028
  - Pistachio: #E0EC89 / PMS 366 / RAL 110 90 40
  - Rosewood: #3C0F11 / PMS 4975 / RAL 3005
  - Moss Green: #173F35 / PMS 567 / RAL 180 30 15
  - Gold: #998542 / PMS 4505 / RAL 1027
  - Teal: #7CE0D3 / PMS 3245 / RAL 6027
  - Cobalt Blue: #0857C3 / PMS 300 / RAL 5015
  - Mustard: #FFBF3F / PMS 136 / RAL 1003
- **Secondary palette:** Black (#000000), White (#FFFFFF), Grey (#9D9D9D), Soft White (#F6F6F6). Black and Grey not permitted as background colors.
- **Colour grouping system:** Colors must connect (documented adjacency rules). Two, three, or four colors per communication. Connecting colors visualized in a circular diagram.
- **Hero pairings:** Moss Green/Pistachio (most ownable), Cobalt Blue/Teal, Rosewood/Poppy.
- **Tints:** Full tint range (5% to 100% in 5% increments) for all primary colors.
- **RAG system:** Positive Green (#0DA20D), Neutral Amber (#FAAA00), Negative Red (#DC000F) -- for data tables only, not brand representation.
- **Gradients:** Three-color gradients only; any palette combination; colors at 60% opacity for harmonization. Not restricted by grouping rules.

## Graphics
- **Grid system:** Two types -- Communications grid (covers, social, presentations) and Editorial grid (interior pages). Margins: 6% of shortest edge. 6 columns, 12 rows for communications; 12 columns for editorial.
- **Special format adaptations:** 3 columns for narrow formats (DL tri-fold); 12 columns for landscape (16:9); 12% margins for very shallow formats.
- **Logo crops:** Portions of logo used as large-scale graphic device on covers.
- **Data visualization:** Comprehensive system including doughnut charts, bar/line charts, tables, maps, timelines, key figures. Exception to color grouping rules (more than four colors permitted).
- **Iconography:** Google Material Symbols (Outlined, Fill On, Weight 400, Grade 200, Optical size 48px). Used sparingly for infographics. Max width = document's smallest margin.

## Photography
- **Four principles (from brand truths):**
  1. Collective subjects: multiple subjects/areas of interest; avoid single isolated subjects
  2. Stronger together: convey collaboration; people interacting, not isolated
  3. Visually powerful: thoughtful compositions, suggest a story, mood, time of day
  4. Warm and personal: authentic, real people, realistic/relatable settings
- **Category libraries:** Private Client, Health & Care, Natural Resources, etc.
- **Anti-patterns:** No isolated subjects, no static/lifeless objects, no staged/uninspiring compositions, no camera-aware subjects with colleagues out of focus.

## Applications
- Brochure covers (lens, gradient, logo crop, photographic, graphic-led), back covers, presentations (16:9), social media, editorial spreads, data visualizations, business cards, email footers.
- **Information system:** Device for specialist divisions (e.g., "Howden Marine," "Howden Specialty") using GT Ultra Median with three-color treatment. Also used for transition branding after acquisitions.
- **Transition branding:** Acquired companies gradually move to Howden name via information system (e.g., "Howden Wallace McLean" then "Howden").

## Tone of Voice
- Not documented as a standalone section in this visual identity guide. Implied through brand truths and the "collective power" narrative.

## Outliers
- Logo that functions as both wordmark and symbol simultaneously, with multiple expression modes (lens, gradient, atmospheric) -- unusually versatile for an insurance company.
- Color grouping/adjacency system is a distinctive approach to palette management -- colors "collaborate" rather than follow simple primary/secondary hierarchy.
- 9pt modular type sizing system (all headings are multiples of 9) is mathematically rigorous.
- Information system as alternative to sub-branding is a pragmatic solution for a complex, acquisitive group.
- Transition branding protocol for acquired companies formalized within guidelines.
- Multi-script typography support (Arabic, Thai, Hebrew) addressed with clear font-switching rules.
- RAG (Red/Amber/Green) data colors explicitly separated from brand palette.
- Photography principles directly map to brand truths, creating strategic alignment.

## Quality Score
**5 / 5** -- Exceptionally thorough and professionally produced brand guidelines for a complex, global insurance group. Every section is deeply considered: the color grouping system, modular typography, multiple logo expression modes, grid specifications, data visualization standards, brand architecture, and photography principles all demonstrate sophisticated brand thinking. The transition branding protocol and information system are practical solutions to real business challenges. Missing only a dedicated tone of voice section, but the visual identity coverage is exemplary.
